docs.text:
Requirement Minimum Lightroom Classic 12.0 macOS 12 Monterey Windows 10 (64-bit)

Lightroom CC is not supported

Adobe's cloud-based Lightroom (the one without "Classic" in the name) has no plugin architecture. This plugin requires Lightroom Classic.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
The plugin doesn't show up in the Plug-in Manager

Lightroom only scans the Modules folder at startup. Fully quit Lightroom (not just close the window) and reopen it. If it still doesn't appear, add it manually via File → Plug-in Manager → Add.

My licence key is rejected

Check for a trailing space when pasting. Keys are 24 characters, grouped in fours. If it still fails, you may have hit the three-machine limit — deactivate an old install from the same dialog.

Does it work with Lightroom CC / mobile?

No. Adobe's cloud Lightroom has no plugin API. Lightroom Classic only.

Can I use it on both my Mac and my PC?

Yes. The three-seat limit counts machines, not platforms.

Processing is very slow

Smart Previews speed things up considerably. Select your photos and use Library → Previews → Build Smart Previews before running a large batch.

How do I get a refund?

Email hello@csiegel.photography within 14 days of purchase. See Licensing.

Still stuck? Open an issue or email me.

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Grab the latest .lrplugin bundle from your purchase confirmation email or the releases page.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
macOSWindows
  1. Unzip the download. You'll get a folder ending in .lrplugin.
  2. Move it to: 
    ~/Library/Application Support/Adobe/Lightroom/Modules/
    Create the Modules folder if it doesn't exist.
  3. Restart Lightroom Classic.

Gatekeeper

macOS may quarantine the download. If Lightroom refuses to load it, run:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Library/Application\ Support/Adobe/Lightroom/Modules/YourPlugin.lrplugin
  1. Unzip the download.
  2. Move the .lrplugin folder to: 
    %APPDATA%\Adobe\Lightroom\Modules\
  3. Restart Lightroom Classic.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. Open File → Plug-in Manager
  2. Your plugin should appear in the left-hand list with a green status dot

If it isn't listed, click Add, navigate to the .lrplugin folder, and select it manually.

docs.title: Activate
docs.text:
1. File → Plug-in Extras → Enter Licence
  2. Paste the key from your confirmation email
  3. Click Activate

Keys are valid for three machines. Deactivate an old machine from the same dialog before installing on a fourth.

docs.title: The basic workflow
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Select photos] --> B[File → Plug-in Extras]
    B --> C[Choose preset]
    C --> D{Preview OK?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Apply]
    D -->|No| C
    E --> F[Export]

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Select one or more photos in the Library or Develop module.
  2. Go to File → Plug-in Extras → Run.
  3. Pick a preset from the dropdown.
  4. Adjust the strength slider.
  5. Click Apply.

Batch processing

Selecting a whole folder works, but processing is sequential. A 500-image batch takes roughly 4–6 minutes on an M-series Mac. Kick it off and go make coffee.

docs.text: Preset What it does Best for Neutral Baseline correction only Mixed batches Warm Shifts white balance +300K Golden hour Cool Shifts white balance −200K Overcast, snow Film Adds grain and a tone curve Portraits

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: Action Shortcut Open the plugin Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P Apply last preset Cmd+Alt+R / Ctrl+Alt+R Cancel a running batch Esc

docs.title: Undo
docs.text: Every change is written as a new develop-history step, so Cmd+Z works normally. To revert an entire batch, select the photos and use Develop → Reset.

docs.title: Adding a new series
docs.text:
1. Create a new file in docs/portfolio/, e.g. street.md, with an empty <div class="gallery" markdown> / </div> block where the photos go

  2. Run tools/build_gallery.py to resize the exports into docs/assets/images/street/ and fill in that block:

    python3 tools/build_gallery.py street \
    --source ~/Desktop/street-export \
    --page docs/portfolio/street.md --dry-run

    Drop --dry-run once the listing looks right. Captions come from each file's IPTC Title, so set those in Lightroom before exporting.

  3. Register the page under nav: in mkdocs.yml

  4. Add a card above so it's reachable from this page

Export sizes

Keep images under ~500 KB each. GitHub Pages has a 1 GB repo soft limit and a 100 GB/month bandwidth limit — full-resolution exports will chew through both. 2000px on the long edge at quality 80 is plenty for web.

A short intro to the series goes here — where it was shot, over what period, what you were chasing.

How captions work

The alt text becomes the lightbox caption automatically (auto_caption is on in mkdocs.yml). Write alt text you'd be happy to show a viewer — it doubles as your accessibility text.

Add { .no-lightbox } after an image to exclude it from click-to-zoom.
